dedupe_keys.name: package delivery quadcopter flight energy measurements

description: Carnegie Mellon University publishes measurements from a DJI Matrice 100 quadcopter carrying small packages on triangular flight routes. The own repository describes 196 flights varying payload, altitude and cruise speed, plus 13 ancillary-power and hover recordings. Payloads range from zero to 500 grams, cruise heights from 25 to 100 metres, and speeds from 4 to 12 metres per second. Position, wind, current and voltage observations are synchronized at a temporal resolution of approximately 5 Hz. KiltHub provides CSV tables and raw and processed ZIP packages under CC BY 4.0 with free access. These controlled experiments can calibrate vehicle-energy and delivery-fleet simulations, extending ground-vehicle demand resources such as data-low-carbon-london-ev-load-profiles. A caveat is that one small quadcopter and a limited flight design do not characterize all delivery aircraft or urban operating conditions. Sensor response and synchronization also affect rapid transients. Only repository metadata and file names were read; flight archives were not downloaded or analysed.
